Windows development preview

Native serial logging, text and severity filtering, command history, auto-save and export. Monitor views currently share one connection and capture.

Download Windows x86_64 · 5.6 MB ↓

Get started

  1. Download and extract the complete ZIP.
  2. Read README.txt and BINARY-LICENSE.txt, then run tracex.exe. This is unsigned; follow your normal Windows security review process.
  3. If the Visual C++ runtime is missing, use Microsoft’s official instructions for the v14 x64 runtime, version 14.44 or newer. It is not included in this ZIP.
  4. Select your serial port and baud rate, connect, and enable Auto-Save if you want text files.
  5. Disconnect and allow saving to finish before closing. Preserve an independent copy of important evidence.

What was verified

48 automated tests, formatting, Clippy with warnings denied and the release build passed. The ZIP was extracted and every packaged file checked against its SHA-256 manifest. These are software checks, not physical-device or crash-recovery certification.

Known limits

  • Transport backlog and in-memory log history are not yet bounded. Long sessions can exhaust memory.
  • Auto-save file operations run in a worker. Some other operations, including connection opening and normal export, can still block the interface.
  • App exit is best effort. Abrupt termination and storage failures can lose unsaved data. There is no crash-recoverable session format yet.
  • Failed auto-save payloads can be exported separately as recovery JSON. Confirmed partial-write byte counts warn about possible duplicates; this is not automatic replay.
  • Text framing normalizes delimiters. Invalid UTF-8 is represented as hexadecimal text and very long records are split. This is not a byte-exact raw capture archive.
  • Windows 11 build/startup checks do not establish compatibility with every adapter or Windows version. No installer, signing or automatic updates are supplied.
